title.narrative: Partnership with UN Office for Project Services in India to Provide Strategic-Technical Support to Jal Jeevan Mission for Achieving SDG6

description.narrative: The support will contribute to the objectives of the Green Strategic Partnership. The purpose of partnership between the Government of Denmark and UNOPS is to provide strategic-technical support to the Indian Prime Minister’s flagship community-managed programme, the Jal Jeevan Mission, which has as its objective that by 2024, all rural households will receive drinking water supply in adequate quantity and of prescribed quality on regular and long-term basis at affordable service delivery charges, leading to improvement in living standards of rural communities. Through coordination between UNOPS and the Embassy of Denmark, it will be ensured that the partnership and the bilateral Indo-Danish cooperation on JJM mutually support and reinforce each other in order to achieve the maximum impact.

title.narrative: • Robust systems in place and functional for planning and implementation of JJM at the National Level • Capacities for social accountability built at PRIs and State level under JJM • Lessons learned, evidence and innovative approaches: identified priority gaps are shared, disseminated and used by implementers to enhance performance of programming • Establish community-based water quality monitoring and surveillance systems and water safety protocols

• VAP (Village Action Plan) prepared and contributed to DAP (District Action Plan) and SAP (State Action Plan) • Schemes are planned and implementation within given timeframe • Community contribution in villages is started as intended. • Ownership and leadership of the JJM program at village level by PRIs ( Panchayati Raj Institutions) • VAP included as part of Gram Panchayat Development plan • PRIs initiating water conservation measures • Water quality testing is being carry out by women groups regularly and remedial measures are being undertaken with PRI support • Learning from the field are being shared and used within project and outside project. • Water quality being monitored by community on periodic basis in villages • Social audit being carried out by village water sanitation committee every quarter

target.value: • Prepared manuals as per numbers shared by the Ministry of Jal Shakti • Prepared 01 training manual, brochures, leaflets • Prepared communication materials (01 documentary on the best practice and components of the Jal Jeevan Mission and 04 short videos/films on work in 11 intervention districts) • 04 documentation/short study on the innovations and good practices from JJM and shared within India and outside India and dissemination of learning from Denmark • Organised 02 National and 04 Regional Rapid Action Learning (RAL) Workshops and documentation of good practices • Write 12 blogs on JJM for learning and sharing • Publication of 04 articles in ‘Jal Jeevan Samvad’ • VWSCs in 95 GPs trained on different themes • Facilitated “Jal Samvad” (water dialogues) in 95 GPs of 11 districts • Prepared Village Action Plan for 95 GPs of 11 districts • 100% FHTC coverage in schools, Anganwadi Centres, Health Centres, GP buildings etc. • 5 women trained on the testing of water quality

actual.value:
Community Lead Action for Sanitary Surveillance (CLASS) - Visible results of the water testing through CLASS were seen creating awareness among households on contaminated water and its impact on health and medical expenses. Training of 5 women each from intervention villages and total of nearly 700 women were trained on testing of bacterial and chemical contamination at source. Many of the women chosen as part of Water Testing Committee were drawn from the concerned VWSCs, ASHA and Anganwadi workers. Many of the women have felt empowered in their role as change makers in their community. They have created awareness on differentiation of clean and contaminated water and identifying quality of water.
UNOPS, through its interventions in the villages and backed with training, has been highly successful in putting communities in the front, developing their understanding around WASH issues and their responsibilities, bringing together service providers and beneficiaries on a common platfor

actual.value: A National Rapid Action Learning workshop was conducted to provide the states with ideas and means to accelerate progress towards the Jal Jeevan Mission and Swachh Bharat Mission (G) Phase-II with prime focus on grey water management. two-day National Rapid Action Learning (RAL) Workshop on Grey water management (JJM & SBM-G) was organized at New Delhi: There were 169 participants from 26 states and 1 UT of India.

Selection of results: Contributed to drafting of Manual for the utilization of 15th Finance Commission Tied Grants to RLBs/ PRIs for water & sanitation, Reforms in the water sector; special booklet in Hindi and English on the JJM. Prepared 4 thematic documentaries on for wider dissemination of JJM over different platforms. The themes were on; community participation, role of water and sanitation committee, preparation of village action plan and skill development. UNOPS prepared 8 training modules for level 3 training of the community and VWSC on different themes.
